title: Ricursive's Ripple-65B Preview is a dense, Apache 2.0 model that tops US open-weight coding leaderboards
subtitle: The ex-Google team pretrained a 65B dense model from scratch for about $32M and claims it beats MoE systems up to 975B on two agentic coding benchmarks.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Ricursive Intelligence released Ripple-65B Preview on November 4. It is a 65-billion-parameter dense language model, pretrained from scratch, released under Apache 2.0, and small enough to run on a single DGX Spark. Ricursive reports 80.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 79.1 on SWE-bench Pro v2.0 Hard, which it presents as the top US open-weight scores on agentic coding, ahead of much larger mixture-of-experts models including Muse Spark Open-816B, Beam-501B, and Inkling-975B. Training cost is reported at roughly $32M. Ricursive's team includes ex-Googlers, and the company credits the Olmo team at Ai2 among its contributors.

The architectural choice is the story. For most of 2025 and 2026, the open-weight race has been dominated by mixture-of-experts systems trained with a trillion or more total parameters but only a fraction active per token. Ripple-65B goes the other direction: fewer parameters, all of them active, and all available to run locally. If the benchmark claims hold up under outside scrutiny, it reopens an argument the field had mostly settled — that MoE was the only efficient path to frontier coding quality.

VentureBeat flagged discrepancies between the launch graphic and the Hugging Face model card on several competitor scores, including Muse Spark Open's result on Terminal-Bench 2.1. That is a reminder that lab-reported numbers at launch are often preliminary and that independent evaluators will produce the harder ground truth over the next few weeks. The Apache 2.0 license means researchers can run those evaluations themselves instead of waiting for permission.

Takeaway for learners: a $32M training run from a small team, released fully open, is the kind of result that quietly resets the floor of what a capable base model costs. If you are learning to build with open-weight systems, this is a good moment to download Ripple, reproduce one or two of the benchmarks yourself, and compare it against a hosted frontier model on your own work. You will learn more from that one weekend than from a month of reading launch posts.
